title: Lecture 5 — polynomials and rational functions
summary: Factor a polynomial to find its roots and read how its graph meets the axis. For rational functions, keep track of excluded inputs even after cancelling common factors.
body:
The saved HT26 course plan assigns Calculus P6 to Lecture 5: polynomials, rational functions, roots and factorisation. This is a study reconstruction for the lecture reported on 7 September, not a transcript; updated Canvas material has not yet been checked.

Start with the degree and leading coefficient of a polynomial. The factor theorem turns a root into a factor, and polynomial division reduces the remaining problem. Multiplicity explains whether the graph crosses or touches the axis. A rational function is a quotient of polynomials: first exclude zeros of its original denominator, then simplify. Cancellation changes the formula, not the original domain.

Continue with Exercise session 5: P6, page 45, exercises 2, 5, 6, 10, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22 and 23. The course plan uses the ninth edition's exercise numbering.
